title: The United States as a superpower
summary: The United States emerged from World War II as one of the foremost economic, political and military powers in the world. The war had created two new superpowers, the United States and the Soviet Union, whose military forces dwarfed all others. The United States became one of the first members of the United Nations, and as the Soviets moved to dominate Eastern Europe, it led the forming of a Western alliance.

uncertainty.note: William T. R. Fox coined 'super-power' in 1944; status was consolidated in August 1945 with victory in World War II and the atomic monopoly.

as_recorded.value: illuminates the new position the United States held as a world “superpower” during the postwar period of 1945–1950, a status based on its vibrant economy and its monopoly on nuclear weapons

importance.justification: American economic and military power shaped world politics after 1945.

related.because: World War II mobilization, the destruction of European and Asian industrial bases, and Allied victory elevated the United States to preeminent global power.
The United States led the creation of the United Nations in 1945 to establish a permanent global framework for collective security and international law.
The development and detonation of the atomic bomb gave the United States a temporary monopoly on nuclear weapons, establishing a cornerstone of early superpower status.
The emergence of the United States and the Soviet Union as rival ideological and military superpowers in 1945 initiated the four-decade Cold War.
The United States spearheaded the international prosecution of Axis leadership, establishing unprecedented standards of postwar international justice.
